items.title: On a symmetric subinterval the conjugate of the transformation is the reflection of that subinterval
items.author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
items.work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 596-602: for a symmetric interval exchange transformation and an alpha-symmetric subinterval, the conjugate of the transformation by the reflection of the whole interval maps the interior of the subinterval onto itself and agrees there with the reflection of the subinterval. The proof (source lines 604-613) is a computation that only becomes possible after two rewritings: the points of the subinterval are expressed as the middle point of the exchanged interval plus an offset, which uses that the subinterval is centred there, and the transformation restricted to the exchanged interval is a translation, so the conjugate of the centre plus offset becomes the conjugate of the centre plus the offset; the identity that the conjugate fixes the centre then turns the result into the reflected point. The statement records neither the parametrisation nor the translation step.
